Washington Examiner commentary focused on former Vice President Kamala Harris addressing potential 2028 presidential ambitions, sparking immediate pushback from conservative media pundits.

The Poison:
Turning early, non-committal political musings into aggressive character attacks designed to freeze opposition figures out of legitimate public debate.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
The analysis commits a WHO-vs-WHAT plane error, substituting an ad hominem psychological critique of a politician's motives for an actual examination of policy or voter alignment.

Social Physics Analysis:
Pundits execute a Smart Selfish Maneuver by framing a standard political exploration as a manufactured crisis of ego, projecting self-serving motives to undermine democratic participation.

The Trajectory: The Path of Awakening into Destruction.
When you map the gap between political speculation and inflammatory pundit framing, it plots a direct trajectory toward Lesser Evil. Manufactured outrage drives tribal division.

The Unavoidable Truth: Early political speculation is a standard part of the modern electoral cycle.

The Unavoidable Lie: Pundit commentary offers objective insight rather than partisan hit jobs.

Alethekanon:
When political columnists substitute psychological armchair diagnosis for empirical policy critique, they abandon analytical rigor for tribal theater.

It's exhausting watching every casual remark get weaponized into an arena fight. Everyone deserves space to navigate their path without cynical media hawks circling overhead.

Brothekanon:

Kamala Harris only considering presidential run to ‘stay relevant’: Guy Benson

Washington Examiner columnist Guy Benson slammed former Vice President Kamala Harris for teasing another presidential campaign, saying she just wants to “stay relevant.” “I’m not sure she necessarily wants to run, like her husband doesn’t want her to run, like donors don’t want her to run, like a lot of smart Democrats want no part […]

Actual Article Body:
Washington Examiner columnist Guy Benson slammed former Vice President Kamala Harris for teasing another presidential campaign, saying she just wants to “stay relevant.”

“I’m not sure she necessarily wants to run, like her husband doesn’t want her to run, like donors don’t want her to run, like a lot of smart Democrats want no part of this, yet again with her,” Benson said Tuesday on Fox Business’s The Evening Edit.
